bib.title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models

question: Can a pre-trained LM be improved at test time, without further training, by interpolating it with a nearest-neighbour distribution over a datastore of context-target pairs?
hypothesis: Learning a prefix representation (similarity between contexts) is easier than predicting the next word, so kNN over LM embeddings should help, especially on long-tail patterns.
contributions: kNN-LM: linear interpolation of a pre-trained LM with a kNN model over LM embeddings, no extra training
New state of the art on WikiText-103 (15.79)
Retrieval over a 3B-token datastore beats training on 3B tokens
Domain adaptation by swapping the datastore
Analysis of key function, k, lambda, precision, n-gram and memorizing-LM alternatives

method.summary: A trained decoder-only Transformer LM is run once over a text collection to store (final-layer FFN-input representation, next token) pairs in a FAISS index. At inference the k nearest keys by L2 give a softmax-over-negative-distance distribution that is interpolated with the LM with weight lambda.

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.size: 103M train tokens; 250K tokens each dev and test

datasets.name: Books (Toronto Books Corpus)
datasets.split: complete books held out for validation/test

datasets.name: Wiki-3B
datasets.split: whole articles held out for validation/test

datasets.name: Wiki-100M
datasets.split: random subset of Wiki-3B, complete articles

models.name: Baevski & Auli (2019) decoder-only Transformer LM
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer; adaptive inputs and adaptive softmax with tied weights on WikiText-103 only

inference.samples: Table 1 reports the median of three random seeds; other tables do not state runs
inference.retrieval: FAISS index; keys are 1024-d inputs to the final-layer FFN after layer norm; index trained on 1M randomly sampled keys with 4096 centroids; keys quantized to 64 bytes; k=1024 neighbours; 32 centroids probed; squared L2 with full-precision keys on WikiText-103, unquantized-FAISS (not squared) L2 on quantized keys for other datasets

parameters.lambda: tuned on validation; 0.25 optimal on WikiText-103, 0.65 best for domain adaptation (Fig 5)

other.datastore build cost: one forward pass over the training set; 103M entries took roughly two hours on a single CPU
other.eval context: 512 tokens scored per example; up to 2560 extra prior tokens (WikiText-103) or 512 (others)

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: exponentiated negative log-likelihood on held-out data

eval.protocol: Held-out dev/test perplexity; lambda tuned on dev; median of three seeds in Table 1.

evidence.quote: we retrieve k = 1024 neighbors, and the index looks up 32 cluster centroids while searching for the nearest neighbors.

results.claim: kNN-LM over the WikiText-103 training set improves test perplexity of the base LM
results.setup: WikiText-103, 247M Baevski & Auli LM, datastore = 103M train tokens, k=1024, median of 3 seeds

results.claim: Adding a continuous cache to kNN-LM gives a new state of the art
results.quote: pushing our state-of-the-art result to 15.79, a gain of 2.86 over the base model

results.claim: A 100M-token LM with a 3B-token datastore beats the same LM trained on all 3B tokens
results.setup: Wiki-100M LM, datastore Wiki-3B, test; Wiki-3B baseline trained 572K steps
results.quote: adding nearest neighbors retrieval over those 3B examples to the model trained on 100M tokens improves perplexity from 19.59 to 13.73
results.note: Wiki-3B-trained LM test ppl 15.17; Wiki-100M LM 19.59

results.claim: Datastore of 1.6B entries already surpasses the LM trained on Wiki-3B; no saturation at 3B
results.metric: datastore size at which kNN-LM beats Wiki-3B LM
results.setup: Wiki-100M LM, datastores randomly sampled from Wiki-3B (Fig 2a)
results.quote: using only 1.6B examples for the datastore already surpasses the performance of the model trained on all of WIKI-3B

results.claim: Adding an in-domain Books datastore to a Wikipedia-trained LM cuts Books perplexity
results.setup: Wiki-3B LM, Books datastore, test; in-domain Books LM gets 11.89
results.quote: Adding kNN search over BOOKS to the WIKI-3B model reduces perplexity by 14 points (to 20.47)
results.note: Table 4 caption says 'improves results by 23 points' but 34.84-20.47 is about 14.4, matching the text; the caption figure is inconsistent

results.claim: kNN-LM also helps on a second domain (Books)
results.setup: Books corpus, 247M LM without adaptive softmax, 1024 context, test
results.quote: Table 2 shows an improvement in test set perplexity from 11.89 to 10.89

results.claim: Best key is the input to the final-layer FFN after layer norm
results.setup: WikiText-103 dev, k=1024, lambda tuned per key
results.table: Table 5, row FFN input after layer norm, column Dev ppl.

results.claim: Even k=8 neighbours reach a new state of the art; more neighbours help monotonically
results.quote: even a small number of neighbors (k = 8) is enough to achieve a new state of the art

results.claim: Full-precision squared L2 beats quantized FAISS distances
results.quote: We found results were improved from 16.5 perplexity on WIKITEXT-103 to 16.06 by computing squared L2 distances with full precision keys

results.claim: Optimal lambda is 0.25 on WikiText-103 and 0.65 for domain adaptation
results.quote: Figure 5 shows that λ = 0.25 is optimal on WIKITEXT-103. However, λ = 0.65 works best for domain adaptation results

results.claim: Interpolating with n-gram LMs gives little gain, so the learned representation matters
results.quote: Figure 7 shows little improvement from using n-gram LMs – 0.2 perplexity points

results.claim: A Transformer trained without dropout memorizes the training set but generalizes badly; interpolating it gives only 0.1 gain versus 1.9 from kNN-LM
results.quote: Interpolating the memorizing LM with the original LM improves validation perplexity by just 0.1 – compared to 1.9 from kNN-LM

results.claim: Building the 103M-entry cache takes about two hours on one CPU
results.quote: for WIKITEXT-103 building the cache with 103M entries takes roughly two hours on a single CPU

limits: Only perplexity is reported; no downstream or generation tasks.
Datastore holds one entry per token (billions of entries) and the authors list reducing its size as future work.
Cost: retrieval at k=1024 took about 25 minutes on the WikiText-103 validation set; no latency or memory figures for the 3B datastore.
Table 1 uses three seeds; other tables do not state run counts or variance.
Similarity function is not trained; the authors name explicit training as future work.
The analysis of why it works is a conjecture (Sec 6), not tested causally.

terms.definition: extends a pre-trained neural LM by linearly interpolating it with a k-nearest neighbors model
key-value store of (context representation f(c_i), next word w_i) for all training examples

code.snippet: p_kNN(y|x) ∝ Σ_{(k_i,v_i)∈N} 1_{y=v_i} exp(−d(k_i, f(x)));  p(y|x) = λ p_kNN(y|x) + (1 − λ) p_LM(y|x)
